title: The braid index of an oriented link
statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For an oriented link $L\subset S^3$, the **braid index** $b(L)$ is the least $n\in\mathbb N$ for which there exists an $n$-braid $\beta$ whose oriented closure $\widehat\beta$ is equivalent to $L$ (equivalently, by Alexander's theorem, the set of such $n$ is nonempty). The braid index is well defined by the closure-invariance lemma: closure depends only on the braid class, so the defining set is a property of $L$ alone.
strategy: Existence for some $n$ is Alexander's theorem; well-definedness of the minimum uses the well-ordering of $\mathbb N$ and the invariance of closure on braid classes. Existence for some $n$ is Alexander's theorem, stated under AC; the closure-invariance lemma is stated under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and is discharged here from AC through the choice-implication bridge.

references.title: Birman and Brendle, Braids: A Survey, Handbook of Knot Theory chapter, author manuscript; section 2 (printed pp. 12-26) and Figures 3-12
